builds.howItPlays: You hold the early turns with cheap spells that draw a card or counter your opponent's spell, then land 7-cost units like Astral Heron, which makes your second card each turn cost 2 less while it sits on a battlefield, and Nasus readies two of your runes each time so you still have answers up. Thousand-Tailed Watcher gives every enemy unit -3 Might the turn it arrives, and once you pay 8 to Empower Nasus, Ascended, he scores you a point each time he conquers a battlefield.
builds.whyYou: You like a patient game where the first few turns are about staying alive and keeping an answer ready for whatever your opponent tries. You enjoy the turn your expensive units finally land and Nasus hands the runes back, so you can still counter a spell afterwards. You don't need to win fast, and you'd rather your cards do the same job every game than gamble on a lucky draw. If a slow build that ends with the biggest units on the table sounds fun, Nasus suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Change 2026-09-25. Relabelled Control to Midrange. Coordinates move from 1/3.5/5.5/6.5 to 3.5/4/7/3.5 (Pace +2.5, Stance +0.5, Complexity +1.5, Variance -3). deckListUrl moves from the bare /decks page to The Big Dog. The old numbers came from reading three guide articles with no deck behind them. The new ones are the mean of three scored decks from the picked Astral Heron Nasus style. Label and coordinates come straight from tools.ts style, and the picks override neither. I didn't recheck outside labels.
Scored decks (tools.ts style: Midrange 3.5/4/7/3.5, labels Midrange, Midrange, Control), pace/stance/complexity/variance:
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/bd343d3e-cd87-4bcd-bb93-576c7ce308d6 The Big Dog - Nasus (Joe Curley; 19 likes, video, Metafy guide; pre-ban), 4/4/7/3.5, Midrange
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/c22812ae-98c0-4470-8df5-beb59fd8567c 8th ValeG $2K Vendetta Cash Cup (Runes & Rift; pre-ban; the result is a title claim I couldn't check, and the deck is scored as the style's medoid), 3.5/4/6.5/4, Midrange
- https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/417234f6-a6b9-4a01-8344-3c0e2b9c4b24 BIRD NASUS (mom sky; pre-ban), 3.5/3.5/7/3.5, rater judged Control (Stance 3.5 with 18 answers per 40)
Adjustments: complexity +0.5 on all three (the Legend readies two runes after each 7+ play, so big turns are sequenced around the refund to hold up reactions). Pace -0.5 on 417234f6 (Forgotten Monument blocks scoring there until turn three, and Sigil of the Storm taxes conquering). Formula-judgment gaps: Pace ran 2.5 above judgment on bd343d3e and 2.1 above on c22812ae. The formula counts 0-Might Scuttle Crab and Steel Paws as cheap attackers, but the Crab is a card-draw unit and Paws waits for its 7-cost Empower. I kept the tags, and each sheet notes the gap.
Cards that decided each Axis:
- Pace: 7 to 10 cards costing 7+ (3 Astral Heron, 3 Thousand-Tailed Watcher, Nasus, Ascended, plus Sprite Queen and Tasty Faefolk in c22812ae), with only Ravenbloom Student as a real cheap attacker.
- Stance: 11 to 18 answers (Defy, Retreat, Zhonya's Hourglass, Bellows Breath, Back Off, Charm, Temporal Breach) against 3 to 6 pressure cards (Ravenbloom Student, Steel Paws). The balance runs -0.14 to -0.41.
- Complexity: 16 to 19 reactive cards (Defy, Discipline, Stupefy, Premonition, Retreat, Hidden Zhonya's Hourglass), Astral Heron's first-card discount and the Legend's refund timing.
- Variance: no luck or swing cards, 53 to 82 percent of each list run as 3-ofs, and 14 to 17 cards that draw.
Legend ability: when you play a unit, gear or activated ability with Energy cost 7 or more, you may exhaust Nasus to ready up to 2 runes.
Also played:
- Sprite Queen Nasus: cheap Poros, Clockwork Keepers and Frostcoat Mothers, then Sprite Queen as the 7-drop. Its decks are https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/2de5e82a-246a-4061-bbe7-5112c53808ee (laggy 'susan', 4.5/5/6/4), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/3b485096-f25b-424c-b9f0-6c76938f3c09 (Best of Barcelona RQ, drinkmaker888, 4.5/5/6/3) and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/e9b5f295-dc15-48cc-83e8-67e9bb05832a (Cameron Hill 'Nasus Tempo', 4/5/6.5/4). All three rated Midrange, style mean 4.5/5/6/3.5, within 1 of this Build on every Axis.
- Guardian Angel Nasus: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/c1bbc195-075d-446c-8b48-ad7cdb8ec057 (tsyco 'Ramp Nasus', 4.5/4/7/4.5, Midrange).
- Applied Researchers Nasus: https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/9ed35f61-f106-40dc-9689-1eec0a250e8a (Rifeli 'ENDGAME - Full Guide', 2.5/3.5/7/4, Control). A lone deck, so it doesn't clear the bar for a Build of its own.
- Merged and unshown: Cameron Hill's 'We will live, they will die.' https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/420d7854-4cc9-45c9-aa97-7ea2c7b0e31d (37 likes, edited 2026-09-23 after the ban; same Heron, Watcher and Nasus plan with Consult the Past and Clockwork Keeper flex slots).
Confidence: high.
Reviewer checks: (1) Nearly every list predates the 2026-09-18 ban, which hit no Nasus card, and no post-ban tournament lists exist yet (the LA RQ is still running). (2) The three old guide URLs are dropped. riftbound.gg (2026-08-20) shows no decklist, and the July riftboundguide.com and skillshotzgaming pages predate these lists. (3) The Metafy guide is Joe Curley's, linked from The Big Dog's deck page, but most of its body is behind a paywall. The fetched page confirmed only a Nasus ramp guide updated 2026-08-20, not the card choices. (4) The Curator's open questions in the picks, about a slot for 420d7854 and about the loosened styles 5 and 6, still need the Maintainer's answer.
